scrubline_decisions_total.help: Flow decisions made by a node's datapath.

scrubline_unowned_flows_total.help: Flows whose destination is not a prefix assigned to this node. A rising value means the steering layer and the fabric disagree about who scrubs what.

scrubline_stage_dropped_total.help: Flows dropped, by the stage that decided.

scrubline_stage_permitted_total.help: Flows permitted, by the stage that decided.

scrubline_stage_dropped_pps_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on flows dropped at this stage. A volume weighting of the drop count, not a packet counter.

scrubline_stage_permitted_pps_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on flows permitted at this stage. A volume weighting of the permit count, not a packet counter.

scrubline_rule_matches_total.help: Flows matched by a rule, including rules that left the verdict to a later rule.

scrubline_rule_drops_total.help: Flows dropped by the rule that decided them. A rule with matches and no drops is seeing traffic it is not acting on.

scrubline_rule_seen_pps_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on flows a rule matched.

scrubline_rule_dropped_pps_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on flows a rule dropped.

scrubline_ml_scored_total.help: Flows scored by the flow model: those a ZC inspect rule sends it, and under scope all whatever the stages let through.

scrubline_ml_drops_total.help: Flows dropped because the classifier scored them at or above the threshold.

scrubline_ml_passes_total.help: Flows the classifier scored below the threshold.

scrubline_ml_model_ready.help: 1 when a fitted flow model is installed on this node.

scrubline_ml_observed_total.help: Flows the flow model scored at or above the threshold and let through, because the policy has it observe only.

scrubline_ml_http_scored_total.help: HTTP requests the layer-7 rules allowed that the request model then scored.

scrubline_ml_http_drops_total.help: Segments dropped because the request model scored a request in them at or above the threshold.

scrubline_ml_http_observed_total.help: Segments the request model would have dropped, let through because the policy or the filter only observes.

scrubline_ml_http_model_ready.help: 1 when a fitted request model is installed on this node.

scrubline_ml_near_misses_total.help: Flows either classifier scored just under the threshold in force here, within 0.1 of it: where traffic tuned to slip past a model lands.

scrubline_ml_tightened_total.help: Times the classifiers' thresholds were lowered a step for a protected prefix because near misses made up a quarter or more of what they scored for it.

scrubline_rate_buckets.help: Sources currently tracked by the ZC behavioral cap.

scrubline_rate_buckets_max.help: Bound on the per-source rate table. At the bound, new sources go untracked and the cap is no longer measuring every source.

scrubline_resident_bytes.help: Memory the node agent's process holds, as the kernel counts it (its resident set). Every table it keeps is bounded, so this levels off under load rather than climbing.

scrubline_offered_pps.help: Packet rate currently offered to a node, averaged over its load window. Load-driven steering reacts to this or to scrubline_surge_pps, whichever is higher.

scrubline_dropped_pps.help: Packet rate a node is currently dropping, averaged over its load window.

scrubline_surge_pps.help: Packet rate offered to a node over the last second. A flood shows here within a second, while the load window's average is still catching up.

scrubline_game_inspected_total.help: Packets a game filter looked at.

scrubline_game_dropped_total.help: Packets dropped because they are not the protocol their port speaks.

scrubline_game_challenged_total.help: Sources sent the protocol's own challenge because they had not cleared the gate.

scrubline_game_uninspectable_total.help: Packets a game filter was given no payload for. The filter never drops on these, so a rising value means the datapath is not supplying payloads and the filter is doing nothing.

scrubline_game_dropped_pps_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on packets a game filter dropped.

scrubline_game_http_requests_total.help: HTTP requests a game filter's layer-7 rules judged.

scrubline_game_http_dropped_total.help: HTTP requests dropped by a game filter's layer-7 rules: a blocked or unknown path, a method, client or body it does not allow, a rate, or a malformed request.

scrubline_game_http_rate_limited_total.help: HTTP requests dropped because their source went over a game filter's requests-a-second limit for the path or the server.

scrubline_game_http_other_total.help: Segments on a game filter's HTTP ports that started no request: the rest of a request, TLS, or another protocol. They pass.

scrubline_game_http_budget_dropped_total.help: Segments a game filter's HTTP rules dropped because everyone together was over a budget and the source held no proof.

scrubline_game_sessions.help: Sources the game filter is tracking through a gate.

scrubline_game_sessions_max.help: Bound on the game filter's session table. At the bound it admits without tracking rather than evicting connected players.

scrubline_game_http_windows.help: Pairs of HTTP rule and source the game filters' request-rate limits are tracking.

scrubline_game_http_windows_max.help: Bound on the request-rate table. At the bound a new source is not rate limited rather than another being forgotten.

scrubline_pulse_active.help: 1 while a protected prefix is under a recognised burst train, including through the quiet stretches between bursts.

scrubline_pulse_peak_pps.help: Heaviest burst measured against a prefix, at sub-second resolution. This is the number a mean hides: a pulse attack keeps its average under the watermark on purpose.

scrubline_pulse_mean_pps.help: Mean rate against a prefix over the pulse horizon. Compare with the peak: a wide gap is the attack.

scrubline_pulse_crest.help: Peak-to-mean ratio of traffic to a prefix. Steady traffic sits near one however heavy it is.

scrubline_pulse_duty_cycle.help: Share of the pulse horizon a prefix saw any traffic at all. A burst train is quiet most of the time.

scrubline_pulse_bursts.help: Distinct bursts counted against a prefix in the horizon.

scrubline_pulse_hold_seconds.help: How much longer the pulse flag stands without another burst. While this is above zero, mitigation does not disengage.

scrubline_prefix_ml_threshold_cut.help: How far under their published thresholds the classifiers drop for this prefix while it is being probed: 0, 0.1 or 0.2.

scrubline_prefix_offered_pps.help: Packet rate arriving for one protected prefix at this node, averaged over the load window. The node-wide rate cannot answer this: a scrubber carries many prefixes at once.

scrubline_prefix_dropped_pps.help: Packet rate being scrubbed for one protected prefix at this node, averaged over the load window.

scrubline_prefix_flows_total.help: Flows decided for one protected prefix.

scrubline_prefix_flows_dropped_total.help: Flows dropped or challenged for one protected prefix.

scrubline_prefix_offered_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on flows arriving for one protected prefix. A volume weighting of the flow count, not a packet counter.

scrubline_prefix_dropped_total.help: Sum of the per-flow rates reported on flows scrubbed for one protected prefix.

scrubline_report_age_seconds.help: Seconds since this node last reported its counters.

scrubline_bgp_announced.help: 1 when a node is advertising a protected prefix, 0 when it is withdrawn. A prefix with no node at 1 is attracting no traffic to the fabric.

scrubline_bgp_prepends.help: AS-path padding on a node's announcement. Higher means the node is a less attractive path and takes less of the prefix's traffic.

scrubline_tunnel_up.help: 1 when a return tunnel is reported carrying traffic, 0 when it is reported down. A tunnel that has never reported is absent from this series rather than reading 0, because no news is not the same as bad news.

scrubline_tunnel_required.help: 1 when a return tunnel must be confirmed up before its prefixes are announced from this node.

scrubline_tunnel_reported.help: 1 when the local provisioner has said anything at all about this tunnel. Zero across the fleet means nothing is reporting, so the control plane cannot tell a healthy return path from a dead one.

scrubline_tunnel_mtu_bytes.help: The tunnel's MTU, after the encapsulation's overhead is taken off the path.

scrubline_tunnel_mss_clamp_bytes.help: The TCP MSS traffic into this tunnel is clamped to. Without it, a customer whose path drops the ICMP that path-MTU discovery needs sees TCP hang on anything larger than a handshake.

scrubline_tunnel_rate_limit_bits_per_sec.help: Clean traffic this node lets down the tunnel: its even share of the tunnel's allowance across the nodes sending it.

scrubline_tunnel_prefixes.help: Protected prefixes delivered over this tunnel from this node.

scrubline_reputation_tracked.help: Source addresses the reputation cache is holding.

scrubline_reputation_tracked_max.help: Bound on the reputation table. At the bound a source takes the ordinary path, so this costs an optimisation rather than a protection.

scrubline_reputation_trusted.help: Sources currently taking the short path because they cleared a protocol gate.

scrubline_reputation_penalised.help: Sources currently in the penalty box.

scrubline_reputation_fast_passed_total.help: Packets taken off the slow path because their source was already verified.

scrubline_reputation_boxed_total.help: Packets dropped at the top of the pipeline because their source is in the penalty box. This is the load the rest of the stages did not have to carry.

scrubline_reputation_promotions_total.help: Sources that cleared a gate and entered the trusted tier.

scrubline_reputation_demotions_total.help: Sources that accumulated enough strikes to be boxed. Counted even when the penalty box is off, which is how it is sized before being switched on.

scrubline_reputation_shielded_total.help: Strikes that landed on an already-verified source and were not acted on. Source addresses are attacker-controlled, so acting on one would let anyone get a real player banned. A rising value is a spoofing attempt or a misbehaving verified client, and both want a human.

scrubline_reputation_freed_total.help: Boxed sources released because their address answered for itself: the origin kept replying to them, or they answered a challenge. Each is a penalty that was cutting off a real client.

scrubline_reputation_full_total.help: Sources the reputation table had no room for.

scrubline_egress_return_packets_total.help: Replies from a protected service observed travelling back through this node.

scrubline_egress_confirmed_total.help: Clients confirmed by sustained return traffic. The service answered them at length, which is the one confirmation here needing no protocol knowledge and the only one an attacker cannot forge from the ingress side.

scrubline_egress_confirmed.help: Clients currently carrying a return-traffic confirmation.

scrubline_egress_clients.help: Client addresses the return-path tracker is holding.

scrubline_egress_clients_max.help: Bound on that table. At the bound a client is simply not confirmed, and under lockdown is not granted grace either.

scrubline_egress_locked_down_total.help: Ingress held back because no return traffic confirmed its source while the prefix was under attack.

scrubline_egress_lockdown.help: 1 when this node is configured to hold back unconfirmed sources during an attack, by mode. A node with every mode at 0 is not running this layer.

scrubline_egress_visibility.help: 1 for the return path this node sees for a prefix. asymmetric means replies are not routed through here — direct server return, or this node is off the return path — and everything depending on return traffic stands down for that prefix.

scrubline_node_prefixes.help: Protected prefixes a node enforces policy on. Zero means the node is enforcing nothing.

scrubline_node_tunnels.help: Tunnels a node's provisioner last reported, by state. A down one withdraws its prefixes from that node; one never reported is not counted.

scrubline_nodes.help: Registered nodes by liveness. A stale node is withdrawn from anycast.

scrubline_policies.help: Policies held by the control plane.

scrubline_announcements.help: Rows in the fabric's BGP announcement plan.

scrubline_prefix_announcers.help: Nodes announcing a protected prefix of the deployed policy. Zero means nothing is drawing the prefix's traffic to the fabric.

scrubline_fabric_recompiles_total.help: Fabric recompiles, including those triggered by a node joining, recovering, or going stale.

scrubline_control_resident_bytes.help: Memory the control plane's process holds, as the kernel counts it (its resident set). It grows with the fabric, the policies and the training set, each of which has a ceiling.

scrubline_control_ml_model_ready.help: 1 when the control plane is publishing a fitted flow model.

scrubline_control_ml_samples.help: Labeled samples the published flow model was fitted to and measured on. Samples carrying an HTTP request train the request model instead.

scrubline_control_ml_validation_samples.help: Samples held out of the fit and scored against. Zero means the set was too small to split.

scrubline_control_ml_accuracy.help: Holdout accuracy of the published flow model.

scrubline_control_ml_precision.help: Holdout precision of the published flow model. A false positive here is dropped customer traffic.

scrubline_control_ml_recall.help: Holdout recall of the published flow model.

scrubline_control_ml_false_positive_rate.help: Share of the clean holdout samples the published flow model drops. Training refuses a model over its limit unless forced.

scrubline_control_ml_max_cut.help: How far under its threshold nodes may hold the published flow model for a target being probed: as far as it stayed within the false-positive limit on clean holdout samples and dropped no known-good one.

scrubline_control_ml_http_model_ready.help: 1 when the control plane is publishing a fitted request model, which needs clean and attack HTTP samples both.

scrubline_control_ml_http_samples.help: HTTP requests the published request model was fitted to and measured on.

scrubline_control_ml_http_validation_sam.help: HTTP requests held out of the request model's fit and scored against. Zero means there were too few samples to split.

scrubline_control_ml_http_accuracy.help: Holdout accuracy of the published request model.

scrubline_control_ml_http_precision.help: Holdout precision of the published request model. A false positive here is a dropped request.

scrubline_control_ml_http_recall.help: Holdout recall of the published request model.

scrubline_control_ml_http_false_positive.help: Share of the clean holdout requests the published request model drops.

scrubline_control_ml_http_max_cut.help: How far under its threshold nodes may hold the published request model for a target being probed.

scrubline_steering_escalation.help: Extra AS-path prepends a node carries because of measured load, on top of what its capacity earns it.

scrubline_steering_load_ratio.help: A node's measured packet rate as a share of its declared packet-rate capacity. Zero when the node declares no capacity to measure against.

scrubline_node_capacity_pps.help: A node's declared packet-rate ceiling. Zero leaves the node out of load-driven steering.

scrubline_api_requests_total.help: Control-plane API requests by route and response status.

scrubline_tunnel_mitigating.help: 1 while an on-demand tunnel is being mitigated on this node, from when its traffic reached a threshold until it has stayed under both for the wave's hold.

scrubline_tunnel_mitigation_wave.help: Which wave of an attack an on-demand tunnel's last mitigation on this node was: 1, and one more for each that started within an hour of the last one ending.

scrubline_tunnel_mitigation_hold_seconds.help: How long an on-demand tunnel's traffic has to stay under both thresholds before the wave's mitigation ends: five minutes for the first wave, doubling with each after it, up to an hour.

scrubline_tunnel_ingress_pps.help: Packet rate reaching an on-demand tunnel's prefixes on this node over the last second.

scrubline_tunnel_ingress_bits_per_second.help: Bit rate reaching an on-demand tunnel's prefixes on this node over the last second.

scrubline_tunnel_attack_pps.help: The packet rate at which this node starts mitigating an on-demand tunnel: its share of the tunnel's threshold.

scrubline_tunnel_attack_bits_per_second.help: The bit rate at which this node starts mitigating an on-demand tunnel: its share of the tunnel's threshold.

scrubline_tunnel_mitigations_total.help: Mitigations of an on-demand tunnel this node has started.

scrubline_tunnel_unfiltered_total.help: Flows to an on-demand tunnel this node let through unfiltered while the tunnel was under its thresholds.

scrubline_crafted_dropped_total.help: Crafted packets dropped, by the check they broke and its class: stack (built to crash or wedge the receiving stack), protocol (breaking the rules of the protocol it claims to be) or buffer (sized to overrun a buffer or reassembly). Any of them rising is an attack no rate would show.

scrubline_crafted_observed_total.help: Crafted packets a check caught and let through because the policy only observes, by check and class: what enforcing would drop.

scrubline_crafted_fragments.help: Fragmented datagrams the node is tracking for overlapping fragments.

scrubline_crafted_fragments_max.help: The most fragmented datagrams a node tracks at once; at the bound the oldest is forgotten.

scrubline_crafted_fragments_untracked_to.help: Datagrams forgotten before their reassembly time to make room, and fragments past what one datagram keeps. Rising steadily means a flood of fragments is cycling the table.

scrubline_crafted_mode.help: 1 for the crafted-packet checks' mode (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then stops a packet built to crash a customer's stack.

scrubline_reflection_dropped_total.help: Answers reflected at a protected address and dropped, by vector: UDP from the vector's port that opens as one of its answers, which nobody behind the address asked for (CLDAP, memcached, SSDP, NTP's monlist and the rest), or for DNS and NTP's time, while the aggregate is flooded with them. Rising means someone is aiming reflectors at a customer.

scrubline_reflection_observed_total.help: Reflected answers, and their later fragments, let through because the policy only observes the vector: what enforcing would drop.

scrubline_reflection_asked_total.help: Answers let through because the protected server had sent their source a query of the vector within the last 30 seconds, so it asked for them.

scrubline_reflection_fragments_dropped_t.help: Later fragments of reflected answers dropped, by vector. They carry no port, so they are told by a source caught reflecting in the last 30 seconds.

scrubline_reflection_sources.help: Sources caught reflecting in the last 30 seconds that the node remembers, so their answers' later fragments are dropped too.

scrubline_reflection_sources_max.help: The most sources caught reflecting a node remembers at once.

scrubline_reflection_sources_untracked_t.help: Sources caught reflecting that the node could not remember because its table was full of others still reflecting; their later fragments are not told. Rising means more reflectors than the table holds.

scrubline_reflection_mode.help: 1 for the reflection guard's mode for each vector (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then stops reflected answers at a customer's address.

scrubline_protocol_dropped_total.help: Packets of an IP protocol no protected address receives, dropped, by protocol: GRE is what botnets such as Mirai wrap their floods in. Rising means one is aimed at a customer.

scrubline_protocol_observed_total.help: Packets of an IP protocol no protected address receives, let through because the policy only observes: what enforcing would drop, by protocol.

scrubline_protocol_mode.help: 1 for the protocol guard's mode (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then stops a GRE flood.

scrubline_ack_flood_dropped_total.help: TCP segments dropped because they belong to no connection the server has, while their prefix was flooded with such TCP: an ACK flood.

scrubline_ack_flood_observed_total.help: TCP segments belonging to no connection, let through because the ACK flood guard only observes: what enforcing would drop.

scrubline_ack_flood_engaged_prefixes.help: Protected prefixes whose ACK flood guard is engaged now: taking more TCP that belongs to no connection than the threshold, or within a minute of it.

scrubline_ack_flood_engage_pps.help: How many packets a second of TCP belonging to no connection a prefix takes before its ACK flood guard engages.

scrubline_prefix_ack_flood_engaged.help: 1 while this prefix's ACK flood guard is engaged, 0 otherwise.

scrubline_ack_flood_mode.help: 1 for the ACK flood guard's mode (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then stops an ACK flood that rates and caps let through.

scrubline_game_http_tls_handshakes_total.help: TLS handshakes (ClientHellos) the filter's HTTP rules counted against the server's rate and budget, which an HTTPS flood is made of; what follows a handshake is encrypted and passes.

scrubline_game_http_slow_dropped_total.help: Segments dropped because their request arrives too slowly: a head unfinished after 20 to 40 seconds (Slowloris), a body under 500 bytes a second (R.U.D.Y.), a client keeping its window too small to read the answer for 30 seconds (slow read), or a source leaving more than 32 requests incomplete at once.

scrubline_game_http_pending.help: Connections the HTTP rules are watching because a request on them is still arriving, or their client advertises a window too small to read the answer.

scrubline_game_http_pending_max.help: The most connections the HTTP rules watch for slow requests at once; one that goes quiet for a minute leaves the table.

scrubline_game_http_pending_untracked_to.help: Connections the HTTP rules could not watch for slow requests because the table was full. Rising means more slow connections than the table holds.

scrubline_reflection_engaged_prefixes.help: Aggregates flooded with answers of this vector the server never asked for, for the vectors it asks itself (DNS and NTP's time): their answers it did not ask for are dropped while this is above zero.

scrubline_reflection_engage_pps.help: How many packets a second of answers it never asked for an aggregate takes, of a vector the server asks itself, before they are dropped.

scrubline_syn_flood_dropped_total.help: Opening SYNs dropped because they came from a source the server has no connection with while their aggregate was flooded with such SYNs: a SYN flood.

scrubline_syn_flood_observed_total.help: Opening SYNs the SYN flood guard would have dropped, let through because it only observes.

scrubline_syn_flood_retried_total.help: Opening SYNs let through during a SYN flood because their connection had sent one a second or more before: a real client retrying, which a forged SYN never does.

scrubline_syn_flood_engaged_prefixes.help: Aggregates whose SYN flood guard is engaged now: taking more opening SYNs from sources the server has no connection with than the threshold, or within a minute of it.

scrubline_syn_flood_engage_pps.help: How many packets a second of opening SYNs from sources the server has no connection with an aggregate takes before its SYN flood guard engages.

scrubline_prefix_syn_flood_engaged.help: 1 while this prefix's SYN flood guard is engaged, 0 otherwise.

scrubline_fragment_dropped_total.help: Fragments of TCP and ICMP dropped, by protocol, which no real sender fragments: fragmented ACK floods and ICMP fragmentation floods are built so to cost reassembly.

scrubline_fragment_observed_total.help: Fragments of TCP and ICMP let through because the fragment guard only observes: what enforcing would drop, by protocol.

scrubline_icmp_dropped_total.help: ICMP dropped, by kind: flood for ICMP over the aggregate's rate, smurf for echo replies to pings the server never sent while flooded with them, error for errors about packets the protected prefix never sent.

scrubline_icmp_observed_total.help: ICMP the guard would have dropped, let through because it only observes, by kind.

scrubline_icmp_limit_pps.help: How many packets a second of ICMP, echo replies aside, an aggregate takes before the rest are dropped.

scrubline_icmp_smurf_pps.help: How many packets a second of echo replies the server never asked for an aggregate takes before they are dropped.

scrubline_icmp_smurf_engaged_prefixes.help: Aggregates flooded with echo replies the server never asked for, as a Smurf attack sends, now or within the last minute.

scrubline_syn_flood_mode.help: 1 for the SYN flood guard's mode (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then holds back a SYN flood the rules let through.

scrubline_fragment_mode.help: 1 for the fragment guard's mode (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then stops a fragmented ACK flood or an ICMP fragmentation flood.

scrubline_icmp_mode.help: 1 for the ICMP guard's mode (enforce, observe or off) on this node, 0 for the others. Alert on off: nothing then holds ICMP floods, Smurf or forged errors back.
